dish.title: Ethiopian Atakilt Wat: Turmeric Cabbage, Potato, and Carrot with Injera
dish.description: A gentle Ethiopian vegetable stew of cabbage, potatoes, and carrots slowly cooked with onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and cumin until soft and sweet, served on injera with a quick tomato and green-chile salad.

recipe_version.title: Ethiopian Atakilt Wat: Turmeric Cabbage, Potato, and Carrot with Injera
recipe_version.description: A gentle Ethiopian vegetable stew of cabbage, potatoes, and carrots slowly cooked with onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and cumin until soft and sweet, served on injera with a quick tomato and green-chile salad.

ingredients.name: jalapeños
ingredients.note: 1 for the stew, 1 for the salad

ingredients.name: injera
ingredients.display_name: injera rounds whose label lists teff, wheat flour, water, and leavening only
ingredients.note: store-bought; required: no barley, milk, or egg on the label

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Slice the yellow onions, mince the garlic, grate the ginger, core the cabbage and cut it into ribbons, and cut the potatoes and carrots. Seed and slice the jalapeños. Dice the tomatoes, chop the red onion, and juice the lemon.

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.body: Heat the oil in a 5-quart Dutch oven over medium. Cook the onions, stirring now and then, until very soft and pale gold, about 10 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, and cumin and cook 1 minute.

steps.title: Braise the vegetables
steps.body: Add the carrots, potatoes, 1 sliced jalapeño, 1 3/4 tsp salt, and 3/4 cup water and stir. Pile the cabbage on top, cover, and cook over medium-low 10 minutes until the cabbage wilts. Stir everything together, cover, and cook until the potatoes are tender and most of the liquid is gone, about 15 minutes more, stirring once.

steps.title: Make the salad
steps.body: While the stew braises, toss the tomatoes, the remaining jalapeño, red onion, lemon juice, and 1/4 tsp salt (overlap stated).

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Lay an injera round on each plate, spoon the atakilt wat and tomato salad on top, and serve the rest of the injera rolled alongside for scooping.
